title: Large-Order Element or Factor
statement: Deterministic output of either an invertible residue with order greater than D or a nontrivial divisor of N.

time.note: Theorem 1.1 v2, not the earlier log^2 N bound. Small D uses the source's regularized logarithm convention, including log log max(D,3); small constant cases are handled directly.

memory.note: Author-stated space bound on p. 4; the paper explicitly omits its detailed space analysis.

success.description: The source's deterministic theorem guarantees the stated output on its declared domain; this is not an independent verification of the proof.

review.scope: Checked the deterministic guarantee and output event in the cited theorem and algorithm.

evidence.locator: PDF/printed pp. 3–4, Theorem 1.1, Equation (1.2), small-D convention and space remark; Section 3 algorithm and proof.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted primary-text transcription; no full-paper audit, global frontier certification or independent implementation run.

limitations: The output may be a large-order element even when N is composite; it is not a guaranteed factorization algorithm.
For prime N the algorithm returns a large-order element, not a primality certificate.
The time expression follows the inspected revised edition; memory is an author statement without a carried-out derivation.
